hints: Look at line 5 of cleanup.sh: rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR/". If BUILD_DIR is ever empty, that quoted string collapses to just the trailing slash — the whole filesystem root.
The fix is one token: "${BUILD_DIR:?BUILD_DIR is empty}" (or set -u earlier in the script) makes an empty/unset BUILD_DIR a fatal error BEFORE rm ever runs — that's ShellCheck's own SC2115 advice.

Write answers.txt with line=5, flaw=empty-var-rm, and fix=... naming the :? guard. Then author hardened.sh from scratch: #!/usr/bin/env bash, set -euo pipefail, the same BUILD_DIR assignment, then rm -rf "${BUILD_DIR:?BUILD_DIR is empty — refusing to rm}/". Test it with BUILD_DIR="" (must abort, no rm) and unset (must still clean normally), then lab check bash L3.2.
